title: GMAT Focus Data Insights Practice Test 18
instructions: Original exam-style practice test with answers and explanations.

questions.prompt:
Five teams, each below a 90% compliance target:

Team A: 400 cases handled, 340 compliant
Team B: 1,200 cases handled, 1,020 compliant
Team C: 250 cases handled, 218 compliant
Team D: 800 cases handled, 712 compliant
Team E: 600 cases handled, 510 compliant

Which team needs the fewest further compliant cases to reach the target?
questions.explanation: Each team needs 90% of its own caseload: Team A 360 against 340, Team B 1,080 against 1,020, Team C 225 against 218, Team D 720 against 712, Team E 540 against 510. The shortfalls are Team A 20, Team B 60, Team C 7, Team D 8, Team E 30, so Team C is closest at 7. Team D has the best compliance rate at 89% but a caseload three times larger, so it still needs more cases than Team C does.

questions.prompt:
Annual figures:

2017: 340
2018: 412
2019: 385
2020: 468
2021: 401
2022: 522
2023: 455
2024: 430

In which year did the figure first rise above the eight-year mean?
options: E. No year exceeds the mean
questions.explanation: The eight years total 3,413, so the mean is 426.63. 2018 reaches 412, still below it, and 2020 is the first year above at 468. The highest year of all is 2022, but the question asks which year first cleared the mean, not which was largest.

questions.prompt:
Five products, ranked separately on sales and on margin, with 1 the best in each case:

Alder: sales rank 1, margin rank 3
Birch: sales rank 2, margin rank 4
Cedar: sales rank 3, margin rank 1
Damson: sales rank 4, margin rank 5
Elder: sales rank 5, margin rank 2

How many products rank in the top three on both measures?
questions.explanation: Top three on sales: Alder, Birch, Cedar. Top three on margin: Alder, Cedar, Elder. On both lists: Alder and Cedar — 2. Birch sells well on a thin margin and Elder is the reverse, so neither appears twice.

questions.prompt: Seven readings are recorded as 14, 22, 19, 27, 22, 31, 16. It is then discovered that two of the readings were written down in the wrong order — the same seven numbers, in different positions. Which statement about the effect is accurate?
options: B. None of the mean, the median, the mode or the range changes
questions.explanation: Each of these four measures depends only on which numbers are present, not on the order they are listed in. The mean adds them all, the median sorts them first, the mode counts repeats, and the range takes the largest and smallest — swapping two entries changes none of those. The readings still total 151, still sort to 14, 16, 19, 22, 22, 27, 31, and still run from 14 to 31.

questions.prompt:
A tile order comes to GBP 1,296.00 in all: a fixed GBP 96.00 delivery charge plus the tiles at GBP 8.00 each.

Select the number of tiles AND the cost per tile once delivery is shared across them.
options: E. The number of tiles cannot be worked out
questions.explanation: Taking the delivery charge off first leaves GBP 1,200.00 of tiles, which at GBP 8.00 each is 150 tiles. Sharing the whole GBP 1,296.00 across them gives GBP 8.64 a tile. Dividing the full total by GBP 8.00 gives 162 tiles and pays for the delivery charge in tiles.

questions.prompt:
A firm employs 480 people. 40% work part time, and 25% of the part-timers are on a job share.

Select the number of part-timers AND the number on a job share.
options: A. 192 part time; 48 on a job share
B. 192 part time; 120 on a job share
C. 120 part time; 48 on a job share
D. 192 part time; 60 on a job share
E. 192 part time; 192 on a job share
questions.explanation: 40% of 480 is 192 part-timers. The job-share figure is 25% of those 192, not of the whole workforce: 48. Taking 25% of all 480 staff gives 120 and applies the second percentage to the wrong group.

questions.prompt:
Two stores last month:

Store One: 8,400 transactions, averaging GBP 14.20 each
Store Two: 2,100 transactions, averaging GBP 62.50 each

Select the store with more transactions AND the store with the higher takings.
options: A. Store One on both measures
B. Store One on transactions; Store Two on takings
C. Store Two on both measures
D. The two stores are equal on both measures
E. Store Two on transactions; Store One on takings
questions.explanation: Transaction counts are given: Store One 8,400, Store Two 2,100. Takings are count multiplied by average value: Store One GBP 119,280.00 and Store Two GBP 131,250.00. The busier store serves four times as many customers but each spends less than a quarter as much, so the quieter store takes more money.

questions.prompt:
A train leaves at 09:38 and runs for 1 hour 47 minutes. The connection departs 23 minutes after that train arrives and runs for 52 minutes.

Select the arrival time of the first train AND the final arrival time.
questions.explanation: 09:38 plus 1 hour 47 minutes is 11:25. The connection leaves 23 minutes later at 11:48 and runs 52 minutes, arriving at 12:40. Leaving out the 23-minute wait gives 12:17 — the whole journey takes 182 minutes, not 159.

questions.prompt:
SOURCE 1 (table): households served — Round P 12,400, Round Q 4,900, Round R 21,000

SOURCE 2 (table): collection crews — Round P 8, Round Q 3, Round R 14

SOURCE 3 (memo): "The extra crew goes to the round carrying the most households per crew it already has."

Which round receives the extra crew?
options: D. The three rounds are equal
E. Cannot be determined from the sources
questions.explanation: Households divided by crews: Round P 1,550, Round Q 1,633, Round R 1,500. Round Q is stretched thinnest and is the smallest round. Round R serves 21,000 households, more than any other, but runs 14 crews to do it.

questions.prompt:
SOURCE 1 (report): "Firms that adopted the framework in 2018 report average growth of 18% since."

SOURCE 2 (note): the survey covers only firms still trading in 2025.

SOURCE 3 (table): 31% of the 2018 adopters had ceased trading by 2025.

Which statement is best supported?
options: A. The framework caused the 18% growth
B. Firms that adopted the framework grew by 18% on average
C. The framework caused 31% of adopters to close
D. The 18% describes the survivors only, and says nothing about the 31% that closed
E. Adopting the framework guarantees growth
questions.explanation: Source 2 says the sample excludes firms that failed, and source 3 says almost a third of adopters did. An average taken over survivors cannot speak for the group that started, so the claim that adopters as a whole grew 18% goes beyond the evidence. Nothing here shows the framework caused either the growth or the closures.

questions.prompt:
SOURCE 1 (table): price a parcel — Courier A GBP 2.85, Courier B GBP 3.40, Courier C GBP 3.05

SOURCE 2 (table): regions covered — Courier A North, South, East; Courier B North, South, East, West; Courier C North, South, East, West

SOURCE 3 (email): "We ship to all four regions and want the cheapest single courier that can reach every one of them."

Which courier should be used?
options: D. All three cost the same
E. Cannot be determined from the sources
questions.explanation: Courier A is cheapest at GBP 2.85 a parcel but does not reach West, so it cannot serve the whole network. Of the two that cover all four regions, Courier B at GBP 3.40 and Courier C at GBP 3.05, Courier C is cheaper by GBP 0.35 a parcel.

questions.prompt:
SOURCE 1 (report): "The department handled 24,000 cases last year, 12% more than the year before."

SOURCE 2 (table): cases handled the year before that: 22,500.

SOURCE 3 (memo): staff numbers were unchanged across both years.

Which two sources cannot both be right?
options: D. All three are consistent with one another
E. Sources 1 and 2 conflict only if staff numbers changed
questions.explanation: A rise from 22,500 to 24,000 is 6.67%, not 12%. For the 12% claim to hold, the earlier year would have to be about 21,429 cases, or this year about 25,200. The two figures cannot both stand. Source 3 says nothing about case numbers, so it is not part of the contradiction.

questions.prompt:
What is the value of the integer n?

(1) n is a prime number less than 20.
(2) n is odd.
options: A. Statement (1) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (2) alone is not sufficient.
B. Statement (2) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (1) alone is not sufficient.
C. BOTH statements TOGETHER are sufficient, but NEITHER alone is sufficient.
D. EACH statement ALONE is sufficient.
E. Statements (1) and (2) TOGETHER are not sufficient.
questions.explanation: (1) leaves 2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13, 17 and 19. (2) alone leaves every odd number. Together they rule out only the 2, leaving seven candidates from 3 to 19. Narrowing a field is not the same as closing it.

questions.prompt:
What is the area of a square?

(1) Its perimeter is greater than 20 cm.
(2) Its diagonal measures 10 cm.
options: A. Statement (1) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (2) alone is not sufficient.
B. Statement (2) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (1) alone is not sufficient.
C. BOTH statements TOGETHER are sufficient, but NEITHER alone is sufficient.
D. EACH statement ALONE is sufficient.
E. Statements (1) and (2) TOGETHER are not sufficient.
questions.explanation: (1) is a bound, not a value, so the area could be anything above 25 square centimetres. (2) fixes it: the area of a square is half the square of its diagonal, so it is 50 square centimetres. The two agree, since that square has sides of about 7.07 cm and a perimeter above 20.

questions.prompt:
How much did a shop take on Tuesday?

(1) It took GBP 1,840 over Monday and Tuesday together, and GBP 900 of that on Monday.
(2) Tuesday's takings were twice Monday's, and Monday's were GBP 470.
options: A. Statement (1) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (2) alone is not sufficient.
B. Statement (2) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (1) alone is not sufficient.
C. BOTH statements TOGETHER are sufficient, but NEITHER alone is sufficient.
D. EACH statement ALONE is sufficient.
E. Statements (1) and (2) TOGETHER are not sufficient.
questions.explanation: From (1), GBP 1,840 less GBP 900 leaves GBP 940 for Tuesday. From (2), twice GBP 470 is GBP 940 again. Each statement alone reaches the same figure, though they describe different Mondays — the question asks only about Tuesday.

questions.prompt:
What is the ratio of boys to girls in a class?

(1) There are 12 more boys than girls.
(2) There are 60 pupils in the class.
options: A. Statement (1) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (2) alone is not sufficient.
B. Statement (2) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (1) alone is not sufficient.
C. BOTH statements TOGETHER are sufficient, but NEITHER alone is sufficient.
D. EACH statement ALONE is sufficient.
E. Statements (1) and (2) TOGETHER are not sufficient.
questions.explanation: (1) fits 13 boys and 1 girl as readily as 36 and 24, and those give quite different ratios. (2) fits any split of 60. Together, boys and girls number 36 and 24, a ratio of 3 to 2. Each statement supplies one of the two equations needed.

questions.prompt:
Which university has the most students for each member of staff?

University | Students | Staff | Research income | Satisfaction
Aldingham | 18,400 | 1,950 | GBP 42.6 million | 78%
Bexley | 6,200 | 890 | GBP 14.1 million | 76%
Cranborne | 31,000 | 2,700 | GBP 96.4 million | 71%
Dunmore | 11,500 | 1,320 | GBP 28.9 million | 83%
Elsworth | 24,600 | 2,050 | GBP 61.2 million | 75%
Fairlington | 4,100 | 640 | GBP 18.5 million | 91%
questions.explanation: Students divided by staff: Aldingham 9.44, Bexley 6.97, Cranborne 11.48, Dunmore 8.71, Elsworth 12, Fairlington 6.41. Elsworth is highest at 12. Cranborne teaches 31,000 students, more than any other, but employs 2,700 staff to do it.

questions.prompt:
Which university earns the most research income for each student on its books?

University | Students | Staff | Research income | Satisfaction
Aldingham | 18,400 | 1,950 | GBP 42.6 million | 78%
Bexley | 6,200 | 890 | GBP 14.1 million | 76%
Cranborne | 31,000 | 2,700 | GBP 96.4 million | 71%
Dunmore | 11,500 | 1,320 | GBP 28.9 million | 83%
Elsworth | 24,600 | 2,050 | GBP 61.2 million | 75%
Fairlington | 4,100 | 640 | GBP 18.5 million | 91%
questions.explanation: Research income divided by students: Aldingham GBP 2,315.22, Bexley GBP 2,274.19, Cranborne GBP 3,109.68, Dunmore GBP 2,513.04, Elsworth GBP 2,487.80, Fairlington GBP 4,512.20. Fairlington leads at GBP 4,512.20 a student and is the smallest university in the table. Cranborne brings in GBP 96.4 million, five times as much in total, but teaches 31,000 students.

questions.prompt:
How many universities are above the median on satisfaction and below the median on student numbers?

University | Students | Staff | Research income | Satisfaction
Aldingham | 18,400 | 1,950 | GBP 42.6 million | 78%
Bexley | 6,200 | 890 | GBP 14.1 million | 76%
Cranborne | 31,000 | 2,700 | GBP 96.4 million | 71%
Dunmore | 11,500 | 1,320 | GBP 28.9 million | 83%
Elsworth | 24,600 | 2,050 | GBP 61.2 million | 75%
Fairlington | 4,100 | 640 | GBP 18.5 million | 91%
questions.explanation: The medians are 77% satisfaction and 14,950 students. Above on satisfaction: Aldingham, Dunmore, Fairlington. Below on student numbers: Bexley, Dunmore, Fairlington. On both: Dunmore and Fairlington — 2. Smaller universities do tend to score better here, but not every small one does.

questions.prompt:
Which university earns the most research income for each member of staff?

University | Students | Staff | Research income | Satisfaction
Aldingham | 18,400 | 1,950 | GBP 42.6 million | 78%
Bexley | 6,200 | 890 | GBP 14.1 million | 76%
Cranborne | 31,000 | 2,700 | GBP 96.4 million | 71%
Dunmore | 11,500 | 1,320 | GBP 28.9 million | 83%
Elsworth | 24,600 | 2,050 | GBP 61.2 million | 75%
Fairlington | 4,100 | 640 | GBP 18.5 million | 91%
questions.explanation: Research income divided by staff: Aldingham GBP 21,846.15, Bexley GBP 15,842.70, Cranborne GBP 35,703.70, Dunmore GBP 21,893.94, Elsworth GBP 29,853.66, Fairlington GBP 28,906.25. Cranborne leads at GBP 35,703.70 a head. That is a third university again: the most students per member of staff and the most research income per student both belong elsewhere, and Fairlington, which wins on research per student, comes only third on this measure.
